report.summary: Analyzed daedalus/structcore/cycles.py (1/1): Tarjan SCC, self-loops, nontrivial components, cycle report. All functions iterative, stdlib-only, deterministic.
risks: cycle_report | medium | Uses import_edges key; if missing, returns empty edges. Index must have correct structure. | Verify index content in integration test.
component_edges | low | Sorts set of tuples; duplicates from multiple src/dst pairs removed by set. | Confirm deduplication is desired.
strongly_connected_components | low | Uses sorted(edges.get(nxt) or ()) each time; could be pre-sorted for performance on large graphs. | Evaluate performance if graph grows.
todos: Consider pre-sorting successor lists in strongly_connected_components for efficiency.
Add unit tests for edge cases: empty graph, single node, self-loop, multi-component.
Verify cycle_report handles missing 'import_edges' key gracefully.

handoff.purpose: Provide iterative, stdlib-only Tarjan SCC and cycle analysis for import graphs.

claims.text: ``structcore`` had **no cycle detection at all**.
claims.why: Claim about past state of the codebase; not verifiable from this file alone.

claims.text: ``import_edges`` / ``import_edges_reverse`` -- the data, complete and correct, including the edges that live inside function bodies
claims.why: Refers to data structures not defined in this file.

claims.text: ``topology.spectral_partition`` builds ``nx.Graph()`` and labels itself 'undirected projection of directed import edges'. It discards DIRECTION, which is the only thing a cycle is made of
claims.why: Refers to code outside this file.

claims.text: ``graph.py``'s ``seen = {rel}`` -- a cycle *guard*, so a walk terminates. Not a detector.
claims.why: Refers to code outside this file.

claims.text: the one structural question the repo actually had -- 'these 13 modules form a cycle, what do I cut?' -- could not be asked of the tool whose job is answering 'what should I distill?'
claims.why: Refers to external context not present in file.

claims.text: It was answered by a 60-line throwaway script instead, and every number in that audit came from code the product does not contain.
claims.why: Refers to external context.

claims.text: Undirected articulation points strand at most 5 of 150 modules (the worst is ``atomic``). Directed reachability loss puts ``core`` at 938 of 3,219 ordered pairs -- **29%**, nearly 2x the next module. ``core`` is a HUB, not a BRIDGE, and an undirected projection cannot see the difference.
claims.why: Refers to external analysis not present in file.

claims.text: Deliberately stdlib-only and iterative
claims.why: Code uses only stdlib (typing, collections, etc.) and iterative loops, no recursion.

claims.text: **stdlib**, because ``topology.py`` returns ``_empty()`` when networkx is absent, and a structural fact as basic as 'is there a cycle' must not depend on an optional extra being installed.
claims.why: Refers to topology.py outside this file.

claims.text: **iterative**, because recursive Tarjan on a 456-node graph with long chains is a ``RecursionError`` waiting for the repo to grow -- and it would surface as a crash in whatever tool asked, not here.
claims.why: Implementation uses explicit stack (work list) rather than recursion.

claims.text: **deterministic**, because these outputs get committed to receipts and diffed between runs. Set iteration order is not a basis for a receipt.
claims.why: All outputs sorted: nodes list sorted, successors sorted, components sorted by size then lexicographically, edges sorted.

claims.text: Every SCC of the directed graph, largest first, each sorted.
claims.why: Result sorted by descending size then lexicographically; each component sorted.

claims.text: Tarjan's algorithm, iterative.
claims.why: Uses explicit stack (work list) and manual index/low management.

claims.text: Nodes are every key plus every target, so a module that is only ever imported still appears -- a leaf is a component of one, and omitting it would make the component count depend on which side of an edge a module happens to sit.
claims.why: Code collects all keys and all targets from edges into 'nodes' list.

claims.text: Ordering is total and content-derived: by descending size, then lexicographically by the component's own members. Two runs over the same graph produce byte-identical output.
claims.why: Result sorted by (-len, comp); components sorted internally; node order fixed by sorted list.

claims.text: Modules that import themselves. Reported separately because a self-loop is a one-node SCC and would otherwise be indistinguishable from an ordinary leaf -- and a module importing itself is a real finding, not a trivial component.
claims.why: Returns sorted tuple of sources where src in edges[src].

claims.text: SCCs that are actually cycles: more than one member, or a self-loop.
claims.why: Filters components: len>1 or (len==1 and member in self_loops).

claims.text: The edges induced by ``component`` -- i.e. the ones a cut must consider. This is the input to any feedback-arc question. Sorted, so a proposed cut can be quoted in a review and re-derived later.
claims.why: Returns sorted tuple of (src,dst) where both in component.

claims.text: Reads ``index["import_edges"]``, which is the layer that ALREADY includes function-body imports -- ``parse._import_records`` walks every node with ``ast.walk`` and records no scope. That is why this is worth computing at all: a cycle detector fed only top-level imports would have reported this repo as acyclic, which is true at import time and false as a change-propagation question. 37% of internal edges live inside function bodies.
claims.why: Refers to parse._import_records and statistics not present in this file.

claims.text: Passing ``index`` avoids a rebuild; omitting it uses the process-wide cache.
claims.why: Refers to .index.cached_index not defined in this file.

observations.what: Module uses only stdlib, no external dependencies.
All public functions are deterministic and produce sorted outputs.
strongly_connected_components builds a list of all nodes by iterating edges twice; could be simplified.
nontrivial_components calls self_loops which recomputes loops from scratch; could be optimized by passing precomputed loops.
cycle_report uses edges.get('import_edges') with fallback to empty dict; if key is missing, report will show zero edges.
component_edges sorts set of tuples; deduplication occurs but order is stable.
